assign.request: Fix the gutter:high finding that catalog-scroll's fix revealed on catalog() pages (/framework/ai/, /framework/ui/, etc) — text sitting 0px from .pages's edge, now visible because the region scrolls. Dispatched by mastermind-layout.
steps: Reproduce: analyze() + shot at both pages, both widths
Implement the fix in catalog.css using the token
Re-run analyze() on the two named pages

assign.now: reproduced: the gutter finding on /framework/ai/ is a real symptom of a deeper regression, not a cosmetic padding miss

log.msg: Reproduced with frame()+analyze() at 1280/3440. /framework/ai/ genuinely has gutter:high (0px, both widths); /framework/ui/ has none — the brief's 'smaller version' read didn't hold up, /framework/ui/ is clean. Traced the flagged region to the app-level nested .pages (path div>div>div from .app), text touching its BOTTOM edge at exactly 0px.

Root cause is NOT a missing gutter — it's a reachability regression. /framework/ai/page.js overrides previews() with a custom .ai-index-rail (ext/AITask/dashboard.js rail()), the only catalog() caller that does. ai.css's board-mode (nothing routed) deliberately sets .ai-index-rail { overflow: visible } with the comment 'a board is not a scrollport — the page scrolls', relying on the outer .pages to grow and scroll. catalog-scroll's new unconditional `.page:has(> .page-catalog) { overflow: hidden; min-height: 100%; grid-template-rows: minmax(0,1fr) }` caps that ancestor's height regardless, so ~15000px of the AI dashboard board is now clipped with NO scroll path anywhere — verified via clientHeight:900 vs scrollHeight:15937 on the page, and outer .pages clientHeight==scrollHeight==900 (it never learns there's more). The 0px gutter is this clip's edge, not a missing token.

assign.outcome: **The gutter:high finding was real but not a missing-padding issue — it was a reachability regression, and fixing it properly (not just silencing it) is what landed.** Traced the flagged node (outer .pages, 0px gap) to a hard clip: /framework/ai/page.js is the ONLY catalog() caller overriding previews() with a custom rail (.ai-index-rail, ext/AITask). Its board state (nothing routed) deliberately sets overflow:visible and relies on the PAGE growing so the outer .pages scrolls it — catalog-scroll's new unconditional `.page:has(> .page-catalog) { overflow:hidden; min-height:100%; ... }` capped that page's height regardless, so ~15000px of the AI dashboard sat clipped with no scrollbar anywhere (verified: clientHeight 900 vs scrollHeight 15937 on the page; outer .pages never learned there was more). Fix: scoped BOTH ceiling rules (the page-level stretch/overflow/grid-rows rule, and .page-catalog-pages's own overflow-y:auto) to `:has(> .page-catalog-pages > .page:is(.active-page, .active-ancestor))` — the SAME routed/unrouted test ai.css already uses for its own board-vs-split column switch. House answer, not an invented token: reused an existing contract instead of adding a --page-pad or any new number. Caught and fixed a second collapse before landing: relaxing the ceiling removed the definite height .page-catalog-pages's flex:1 1 0 needed, collapsing it to a true 0x0 box at the <64em strip breakpoint on EVERY catalog caller's default view (zero-size, LayoutTool caught it immediately) — fixed by narrowing the scoped overflow-y:auto rule with the identical test so the two rules can't disagree. Verified: gutter finding gone (0 across all 8 catalog() callers x 3 widths), zero-size gone, zero new unreachable findings, routed/split state unchanged (still bounded, still self-scrolling, spot-checked /web/nav/sidebar/ and /framework/ai/2026-08-16/). /framework/ai/ score 70→82/B (1280), 49→61/D (3440, 2 remaining highs are pre-existing unrelated 'measure' long-line findings). Found but did NOT fix, out of this module's fence: /framework/ai/<day>/ is unreachable at <64em while ROUTED — confirmed via git-stash to predate catalog-gutter entirely (a third pre-existing regression from the same ceiling); root cause and exact fix recorded in ext/catalog/readme.md + doc/decisions.md, belongs in ai.css not catalog.css. Landed in ext/catalog/catalog.css, readme.md, doc/decisions.md.
